settings.title: Battery data for Google Maps (EV energy model)
settings.description: Sends Maps the battery's real energy, its learned usable capacity, charge curves and the outside temperature every 5 s during Android Auto, for its arrival charge and charging stops. Needs an Android Auto library build the mod can patch: the ones it ships a patch for (Ioniq 5 and EV6 US 260507, EV6 Canada 260206, Ioniq 6 US 260903 and Canada 260206), or any build with the same code, found by HMG-API after 1.1.0-rc.2. Made for E-GMP (Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6, EV6). Other EVs (Kona Electric, Niro EV, Soul EV) start from E-GMP values and need time to learn: highway driving at 60 km/h or more for the car's consumption (most of the way after about 200 km, with "Learn this car" on), and a charge above 60% for its battery size. Until then Maps' arrival charge can be off. Charge times start from E-GMP's, too fast for 400 V cars, and learn from the car's DC stops at chargers Maps guided it to (with "Learn this car" on).

settings.title: Maps' battery % matches the car's
settings.description: Sends Maps how the car's battery % relates to the battery's energy (Android Auto sensor 26), so the percentages Maps shows (now, on arrival, at charging stops) match the dash. On E-GMP the energy runs out at about 2% on the dash, so without it Maps reads up to 2 points low near empty. Needs the energy model on and a library build whose recipe takes sensor 26 (Ioniq 5 and EV6 US 260507, EV6 Canada 260206; Ioniq 6 US 260903 and Canada 260206, not yet checked on one).

settings.title: Arrive at charging stops with at least (%)
settings.description: Google Maps plans its charging stops so the car arrives at each with at least this battery % (1-50). 0 (the default) leaves Maps' own setting. Sent with the battery % data (Android Auto sensor 26), so it needs the energy model on and the same library builds as "Maps' battery % matches the car's". Changes apply at once if that sensor was already on this session, otherwise from the next Android Auto connection.

settings.title: Arrive at the destination with (%)
settings.description: Google Maps plans the trip so the car reaches the destination with this battery % (1-100). 0 (the default) leaves Maps' own setting. Same needs as the setting above.

settings.title: I carry a NACS (Tesla) adapter
settings.description: Tells Maps the car can also use NACS (Tesla Supercharger) plugs, besides CCS1 and J1772, so its charging stops can include Superchargers that take adapters. Needs a library build whose patch takes it (Ioniq 5 and EV6 US 260507). Not yet checked on a car: see Maps' Compatible plugs screen.

settings.title: Winter model for Maps (test)
settings.description: Also sends Maps the live heater and climate power, charge times for a cold pack (by the battery temperature it now gets), and a battery preconditioning model (assumed E-GMP values). For cold-weather arrival charge and charging-stop times. Untested on Maps: compare its plan with this off on the same route. Needs the energy model on.

settings.title: Test: flat block 4 (charge or regen limit?)
settings.description: For one car test only: sends a flat 150 kW in the energy model's block 4, which Google's schema calls the regen limit and egmp fills with the charge curve. If Maps' planned charging minutes change, block 4 is a charge limit. Leave off otherwise.

settings.title: Precondition the battery on the way to a DC fast charger
settings.description: When Maps (Android Auto) guides to a charging stop, asks the car to warm or cool the battery, with the real distance and time to it (the thresholds are below). Off too when the car's own Battery Conditioning setting is off. Needs the route data the Wireless CarPlay + Android Auto mod's turn-by-turn adds.

settings.title: Precondition for chargers faster than (kW)
settings.description: Maps' charging stops above this power count (0-400; 50 by default, so DC fast chargers only). Applies at once, to the current route too.

settings.title: Start when the charger is this many minutes away
settings.description: By Maps' remaining time (5-180; 60 by default). The car's battery system then times the heating from the distance and time it's sent. HMG-API stops a request if the car's indicator isn't on within 2 minutes, and automatic starts then wait for a manual one, so a shorter window (20-30) is safer until HMG-API lets a routed request wait for the car.

settings.title: Arrived within (metres)
settings.description: Closer than this to the charger, preconditioning stops and doesn't start (50-2000; 200 by default).

settings.title: Starts per route at most
settings.description: If the car keeps ending the request (1-10; 3 by default).

settings.title: Battery level, range and odometer for Android Auto apps
settings.description: Sends the battery %, the range the cluster shows and the odometer to the phone every 5 s during Android Auto, as Android Auto's fuel and odometer data. Apps that read the car's data, such as A Better Route Planner, show the live battery level. Needs no library patch.

settings.title: Learn this car: highway consumption and DC charging
settings.description: Compares the energy model with this car's own steady highway drives (10 km stretches at 60 km/h or more, from the EV log) and scales the model's road load to match, between 0.7x and 1.3x. Also learns how fast the car really DC fast-charges in each 10% SOC band, from stops at chargers Maps was guiding to where the car, not the charger, set the pace, so Maps' charge times follow the car's own stops. Takes effect at the next Android Auto session. Turning it off forgets what it learned. Needs EV logs on.

settings.title: EV logs
settings.description: Logs battery, charging, climate and Maps' route plan whenever the head unit is on (no location or time of day). Copied to any USB drive that has an egmp-aa-ev-logs folder.
